summary: Backend regression tests for the deleted_seeds fix (user bug: 'Erica Elevated Peptide' resource kept coming back after delete). Wrote 5 pytest tests covering the exact scenarios requested. All 5 passed.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 1256 lines — consider splitting resources/vendors/peptides/socials/settings/seed logic into separate modules for maintainability (per code review guideline: >700 lines should be split).

deleted_seeds mechanism works but does not have an admin endpoint to *restore* a killed seed title. If admin ever wants a seed back after purging it, they must recreate via POST (which does work). Consider adding DELETE /api/deleted_seeds/{title} for future flexibility.

Seed matching uses exact title equality (`db.resources.find_one({title: r['title']})` and `deleted_seeds` lookup by title). Any renamed seed record could theoretically be resurrected — acceptable for now, but worth documenting.
seed_data_creation: Test 3 created a new 'My Peptide Community — Erica's Elevated Life' resource, then deleted it (verified stays gone across restart). Test 5 deleted 'How to Read a COA' and re-created it via POST as cleanup so preview stays healthy. Final GET /api/resources confirms: Erica absent, COA + Peppy Pens present (7 resources total).
context_for_next_testing_agent: The deleted_seeds regression is fully covered by /app/backend/tests/test_deleted_seeds.py. Each restart-test calls `sudo supervisorctl restart backend` and waits for readiness. Tests are idempotent and self-cleaning. Preview verified healthy after run.
verified_scenarios: GET /api/resources does not contain any Erica+Elevated resource
After sudo supervisorctl restart backend, Erica still absent (core regression)
Admin can create + delete a new Erica-titled resource; after restart it stays gone (title-based blacklist works)
Other seeded resources ('How to Read a COA', 'Peppy Pens') still seed normally
Generic proof: deleted 'How to Read a COA', restarted backend, verified absent, then restored via POST — mechanism works for any seed title, not just Erica
